summary: Customer needs strict EU-only processing for a subset of ML workloads. Discussion covered region pinning, cross-border processing exceptions, sub-processor disclosures, KMS/HSM architecture, audit logs retention, and contractual remedies. Redwood proposed Private deployment or Dedicated capacity with region pinning, explained fallback policies, and committed to share architecture and SOC2/ISO artifacts.
transcript:
Header: 2026-04-15 15:00 UTC | Duration: ~55m | Attendees: Alyssa Chen (Redwood AE), Marcus D'Souza (Redwood SE), Emma Fischer (Acme Head of Security), Liam O'Connor (Acme Cloud Architect), Sofia Martinez (Acme Legal), Daniel Weber (Acme Platform)

[00:00] Alyssa: Hey everyone, thanks for taking the time. Quick roll call, then we'll go through our data residency and region pinning approach and answer any compliance Qs.
[00:12] Emma: Hi, Emma here. Main ask from our side is — we have a set of workloads that must remain and be processed in the EU only, no cross-border processing, and we need contractual guarantees and technical enforcement.
[00:27] Marcus: Totally understood. Today we'll run through options: Hosted with EU-only routing, Dedicated reserved capacity in EU, and Private deployment into your VPC or on-prem. We'll also cover KMS, audit logs, and sub-processor disclosure.
[00:40] Liam: For clarity, when you say Hosted with EU-only routing, is that purely a routing preference or is there any possibility of failover to US regions if capacity is low? That's a hard no for us unless it's explicit and we can opt in.
[00:55] Marcus: Right, so by default hosted can be pinned by region — EU region pinning means we route requests to EU-hosted nodes only. We do have fallback policies for availability but those are configurable per-customer; we can disable cross-border fallback for the EU-only workloads. There's a nuance though: some managed sub-systems, like telemetry or analytics, may still aggregate across regions unless you opt into Private.
[01:18] Emma: That nuance is important. Our legal/compliance team won't accept metadata leaking to US analytics.
[01:25] Alyssa: Understood — we can mark that in the DPA and isolations. For absolute isolation we typically recommend Redwood Private or a Dedicated EU-only cluster with contractual controls.
[01:36] Sofia: From a legal perspective, we need to confirm the list of sub-processors and whether any of them process data outside the EU. Also want to see SCCs and proof of adequate safeguards.
[01:49] Marcus: Yes, we have a maintained sub-processor list. For Hosted we use cloud infra providers and a few telemetry vendors; we will share the list and highlight any cross-border processing. For Private deployments the sub-processors are limited — typically the customer manages the infra and Redwood acts as control plane with minimized PII access.
[02:10] Daniel: If we go Private inside our VPC, how do keys work? We need customer-managed keys, ideally HSM-backed. Do you support bringing your own key?
[02:22] Marcus: We do. We support KMS integrations — AWS KMS, GCP Cloud KMS, and HSM via PKCS#11 for on-prem. For Private deployments you can configure BYOK so that encrypted model weights and request payloads are inaccessible to Redwood without customer consent. A couple of small caveats on session keys and ephemeral caches which we can document.
[02:45] Emma: Can audit logs be kept in-region and have separate retention policies?
[02:51] Marcus: Yes, audit logs can be configured to ship to your EU logging cluster or to a customer-managed S3/GCS bucket in region. Retention policies are configurable per-route. There might be a small metadata index kept for routing that lives in the control plane; we can carve that out in the architecture and put contractual guardrails around it.
[03:14] Liam: What about model caching and KV cache behavior — could cache keys inadvertently be stored in other regions?
[03:22] Marcus: Great question; our serving runtime has per-cluster KV caches. If you're on a EU-only cluster those caches are local to EU nodes. If you're in Hosted with fallbacks enabled, there is a risk of remote cache population. We'll share recommended configs which disable cross-region cache warming for EU-only workloads.
[03:43] Emma: Are there any cases where support personnel might need to access EU data from outside EU? That's usually a blocker for us.
[03:51] Alyssa: Support access is governed by RBAC and SSO; we can restrict access to named engineers and require VPN + IP whitelisting. For Private deployments, remote access is customer-controlled and typically goes through your bastion. For Hosted we log and can restrict support sessions, and provide jumpHost explanations in the security pack.
[04:12] Sofia: We need to see SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001 evidence. Also, encryption at rest and in transit specifics and any encryption-in-use for model execution.
[04:22] Marcus: We'll share the SOC 2/ISO certs and the attestation summary. For encryption: TLS in transit is standard, rest is AES-256 for disks. Execution-level encryption (confidential compute) isn't default; however, for Private/on-prem you can run inside your secure enclaves. We also provide tokenization and request-level redaction hooks.
[04:44] Emma: Regarding sub-processors — can you commit to notifying us 30 days prior to adding any new sub-processor who will process EU data?
[04:52] Alyssa: Yes, we can include a notification clause in the DPA. Standard process is notice plus opt-out for certain classes; we'll mark that as a negotiable clause.
[05:03] Daniel: What about backups and cross-region replication for disaster recovery? We need backups to also be EU-confined for the EU-only dataset.
[05:12] Marcus: Backups replicate in-region only if you configure region pinning; global backups are off by default for pinned clusters. For Hosted customers that choose cross-region DR we document that explicitly and make it opt-in.
[05:25] Liam: Does Redwood keep any PII in logs or traces? We try to avoid that.
[05:32] Marcus: By default tracing masks PII and request payloads are redacted unless you opt-in to full-text logs. We can provide the exact regex patterns and redaction config used.
[05:46] Emma: Can you explain the routing policy syntax? I want something deterministic: EU-only for model endpoints A,B,C, and fail open to Dedicated EU instances only, not to US.
[05:58] Marcus: Sure — routing policies are per-route config. Example: route.policy.region = eu-west-1; route.policy.fallback = none or fallback = dedicated-eu; fallback = global could trigger cross-border. We'll send sample route YAML. Also, you can pin per-model and per-customer.
[06:20] Sofia: Legal wants to confirm liability limits if there is an inadvertent cross-border transfer.
[06:26] Alyssa: Standard clauses in our DPA include incident notification timelines and indemnities tied to sub-processor misconfiguration; we can surface specific language for cross-border incidents. We'll flag this for legal review.
[06:42] Emma: How long are audit logs retained? We need 7 years for some financial traces.
[06:48] Marcus: Our platform supports long-tail retention. For Hosted we can ship logs to your long-term store; retention is customer-controlled. For Dedicated/Private we don't enforce retention. We also provide compressed export tools.
[07:05] Liam: On the technical side — latency and model updates — if we pin to EU-only, how do you handle model rollouts and compatibility with quantized weights? Any chance a rollout forces a cross-region dependency?
[07:18] Marcus: Model rollouts are orchestrated within the chosen cluster. For EU-only Dedicated clusters, updates roll out within-region. We also avoid pulling remote artifacts except from your allowed artifact stores; you can host the model artifacts in your EU artifact repo.
[07:33] Emma: Any mention of sub-processors that are US-based analytics vendors — can you disable telemetry entirely for our EU-only group?
[07:41] Marcus: Yes, telemetry can be disabled or routed to your EU analytics. We'll show how to toggle that per-customer.
[07:51] Daniel: A quick ops question — do you support SAML/SSO for RBAC and can we integrate with our IdP hosted in EU?
[07:58] Alyssa: Yes, SSO via SAML/OIDC is supported. You can map groups to RBAC roles and enforce conditional access. We'll include a short SSO mapping example.
[08:12] Emma: Can we get a written statement about no sub-processor changes without notice and a list of current sub-processors including region of processing?
[08:20] Alyssa: We'll attach the current sub-processor registry and mark any EU-only flags.
[08:26] Sofia: From a contractual standpoint we will want SCCs and probably a data processing amendment that reflects EU-only processing for specific endpoints.
[08:34] Alyssa: Agreed — we'll draft DPA language for EU-only endpoints and include options for Private deployment or Dedicated EU-only capacity in the quote.
[08:44] Marcus: One more technical note: for customer-managed KMS we have envelope encryption where the master key never leaves your HSM. We support rotation and key revocation; when a key is revoked, ephemeral caches are invalidated across the cluster. We'll provide the rotation semantics doc.
[09:05] Liam: How about support for data residency in specific EU countries vs broader EU?
[09:12] Marcus: We can pin to a specific region (eu-west-1) or to EU as a whole; some customers require country-level pinning and we can accommodate that with Dedicated or Private. Hosted EU-scope is typically multi-AZ but within the jurisdiction you select.
[09:28] Emma: Let's talk incident response — if there's a suspected cross-border leak, what's your notification SLA and investigation steps?
[09:36] Alyssa: We have a 72-hour incident notification baseline for security incidents and faster for critical PII exposure. We'll provide our IR playbook summary and the escalation contacts.
[09:48] Sofia: We need to see proof of penetration testing and results summary.
[09:52] Marcus: We'll include the latest pen test summary and remediation list.
[10:00] Daniel: One last technical concern — if you route EU requests to EU model variants, will the embeddings or vector indexes ever be exported to US compute for reindexing?
[10:09] Marcus: Vector stores are per-cluster; we can ensure vectors for EU pinned workloads remain in EU-only indexers or ship snapshots to your in-region store. We'll document vector retention and export controls.
[10:22] Emma: OK, can you summarize the path forward?
[10:25] Alyssa: Sure. Summary: 1) We'll send SOC2/ISO docs and sub-processor registry; 2) Marcus will send technical runbook on region pinning, KMS, and routing policy; 3) we'll draft DPA language for EU-only endpoints and notification clause; 4) schedule follow-up to review Private deployment architecture.
[10:44] Sofia: That works. Legal will prepare questions based on the DPA draft.
[10:48] Alyssa: Great. Thanks everyone. We'll target the artifacts by next week.
[10:53] Meeting ends.
